chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Stoning is the greater Hadd of Allah, and whipping is the lesser Hadd of Allah. So when a married man commits adultery, he is stoned and not whipped.

key_terms.الجلد: Jald — flogging/whipping; 100 lashes prescribed for an unmarried person who commits zina
key_terms.الحد: Hadd — a fixed, divinely ordained corporal punishment prescribed in Islamic law
key_terms.الرجم: Rajm — stoning; the prescribed capital punishment for zina committed by a muhsan (married) person
key_terms.المحصن: Muhsan — a person who is or has been in a valid marriage, which is the condition triggering the penalty of rajm
key_terms.زنى: Zina — illicit sexual intercourse (adultery or fornication)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between stoning (rajm) and flogging (jald) in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes the two primary corporal penalties (hudud) for zina (unlawful sexual intercourse) in Islamic law: stoning (rajm) as the greater punishment for married (muhsan) offenders, and flogging (jald) as the lesser punishment. This hadith establishes that for a married man who commits zina, only stoning applies — not both penalties combined. The Imam frames these as divinely ordained punishments, ranking them by severity and attributing their authority directly to God.
